the role of NOD-like receptor X1 (NLRX1) in regulating TNF-α mediated mitochondrial-lysosomal catabolism and its role in modulating invasion and metastatic capability in triple-negative breast carcinoma.
the role of NOD family receptors in regulating mitochondrial and lysosomal turnover and its implication on breast cancer progression.

NLRX 1 plays an important role in regulating the TNF-α mediated mitochondrial turnover and lysosomal function and its loss leads to impaired autophagy flux, OxPhos activity, invasion and metastasis potential of triple negative breast cancer cells.

NLRX-1 regulates the mitochondrial bioenergetic potential and lysosomal function in presence of TNFA to maintain the invasion and metastatic potential in breast cancer cells.
, NLRX1 is an important regulator of mitochondrial and lysosome function during inflammation, and hence the invasive and metastasis potential of breast cancer.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the NLRX1 mediated crosstalk of mitochondria and lysosome regulates the invasive and metastasis potential of triple-negative breast cancers.
NLRX-1 regulates mitochondrial function to maintain mitochondrial-lysosomal catabolic function, which is essential for the invasive and metastasis potential of breast cancer.
